thread.title: Child Who Went Missing For 7 Years Found Alive Several States Away, Officials Say
thread.title_full: Child Who Went Missing For 7 Years Found Alive Several States Away, Officials Say

author: Fiona McLoughlin
title: Child Who Went Missing For 7 Years Found Alive Several States Away, Officials Say
text:
A Georgia child who went missing seven years ago was found alive in Colorado on Feb. 23, officials announced Wednesday.
Abdul Aziz Khan went missing when he was seven years old after his mother allegedly abducted him in Atlanta on Nov. 27, 2017, according to a Douglas County Sheriff’s Office (DCSO) press release. The mother was a non-custodial parent, authorities said.
The now 14-year-old was located and recovered by DCSO deputies responding to a trespassing call on Feb. 23 in Colorado. Responding officers found two individuals who had allegedly entered a vacant, for-sale property. They were in the process of burglarizing it, officials said. The responding deputies also found two children in a car parked in the residence’s driveway, according to the DCSO.
A man and woman left the house, claiming to be connected to the home’s realtor. Deputies then spent four hours working to determine the identities of the two suspects.
“The female was finally identified as 40-year-old Rabia Khalid, who had an active warrant for kidnapping. Continued research verified the older child on scene was the victim of the kidnapping and is currently 14 years old,” the DCSO said. (RELATED: Family Finds Man 73 Years After Woman Allegedly Kidnapped Him)
Law enforcement arrested Khalid and Elliot Blake Bourgeois, 42, and booked them on multiple charges, including Second Degree Kidnapping , Trespassing, Identity Theft , Forgery and Providing False Information to Authorities, the DSCO said. Both of their bonds were set at $1 million.
Authorities placed both children into protective custody and the identity of the younger child was withheld by the sheriff’s office, according to the DCSO. The court will determine where to place the children.
“We’re overwhelmed with joy that Aziz has finally been found. We want to thank everyone for their support over the last seven years. We specifically want to recognize the Douglas County Sheriff’s Office for their exceptional work in solving this case,” Khan’s family said in a statement. “Now, as we navigate the next steps, we ask for privacy so that we can move forward as a family and heal together.”
“I couldn’t be prouder of the work done by our team; this case highlights the commitment of our officers to seek justice and protect the most vulnerable. It’s a reminder of the incredible difference our work makes in the lives of those we serve,” DCSO Sheriff Darren Weekly said.
The sheriff’s office said an investigation remains underway as officials work to collect more information to resolve the case .
Khan’s disappearance was featured in an episode of Netflix’s Unsolved Mysteries series. U.S. Marshal Enix Smith III for the Eastern District of Louisiana thanked Netflix, among other organizations, for bringing the public’s attention to the case.
“I extend my sincere gratitude to all involved in the recovery effort, especially the authorities in Douglas County, Colorado for their swift and effective actions. Also, we would like to thank NCMEC, Netflix’s Unsolved Mysteries, and Crimestoppers GNO for directing the public’s attention to this matter,” he said.
